texts.facts: The second respondent in the writ petition is the writ appellant before this Court. 2. The first respondent herein Mrs.D.Eswari, being a senior citizen, lodged a complaint under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 before the designated Tribunal/Revenue Divisional Officer. The complaint filed by the senior citizen reveals that the appellant, who is none other than the son of the senior citizen, fraudulently registered settlement deeds in his favour by coercion and thereafter neglected the senior citizen. In the complaint, it is stated that the appellant has not even provided medical treatment to the senior citizen and she is suffering to meet out the medical expenditures, as she has no other source of income, except the property which has been settled in favour of the appellant. The allegation in the complaint is that the appellant is having ____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 22/04/2025 01:23:58 pm ) illicit relationship and neglected his own wife and children. Several other allegations are also raised against the appellant by the senior citizen for the purpose of annulling the settlement deeds executed by the senior citizen in favour of the appellant. 3. The appellant filed a reply stating that he would meet out the maintenance expenditures of his mother/senior citizen. However, he made a statement before the Tribunal that he would meet out the medical expenditures of the senior citizen. Admittedly, the subject properties are the self-acquired properties of the senior citizen. It is clearly stated in the settlement deeds that the appellant being the elder son of the senior citizen, out of love and affection and considering the future life of the appellant, the properties belonging to the senior citizen were settled. The condition need not be expressly made and it is sufficient if it is impliedly made. The consideration for execution of the settlement deeds by the senior citizen was the love and affection and therefore the appellant is obligated to maintain the senior citizen till her lifetime. ( Uploaded on: 22/04/2025 01:23:58 pm ) declaring the settlement deeds as null and void and sham and nominal. The appellant was directed to handover vacant possession of the lands to the senior citizen. Hence this appeal.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for appellant would mainly contend that the appellant is ready and willing to maintain the senior citizen and to provide all amenities. 6. Mere statement before the Court would be insufficient, since there was a strained relationship between the parties. The senior citizen made a complaint that the appellant has not even maintained his own wife and children. She is suffereing to even meet out the medical expenditures and unable to eke out her livelihood. The relief granted by the Appellate Tribunal to pay a sum of Rs.5,000/- as monthly maintenance would be insufficient and considering the fact that the settlement deeds were executed by coercion, the writ Court has rightly [LEAKAGE_MASK] the order and declared the settlement deeds as null and void. This Court has elaborately considered the legal principles, governing the provisions of the Senior Citizens Act, particularly in the case of S.Mala vs. District Arbitrator and District Collector, Nagapatinam District (W.A.No.3582 of 2024 dated 06.03.2025). The essence of law is to serve and secure social solidarity, ensuring that individuals fulfil their obligations as members of society. 22. The Supreme Court, in F.Francis Coralie Mullin vs. Administrator, Union Territory of Delhi4, expanded the scope of Article 21 of the Constitution of India, recognizing that: "We think that the right to life includes the right to live with human dignity and all that goes along with it, namely, the bare necessaries of life such as adequate nutrition, clothing and shelter and facilities for reading, writing and expressing oneself in diverse forms, freely moving about and mixing and commingling with fellow human beings. 25. The law has been made in order to cast an obligation on the persons, who inherit the property of their aged relatives to maintain such aged relatives and also proposes to make provisions for setting-up oldage homes for providing maintenance to the indigent older persons and also to provide better medical facilities to the senior citizens and provisions for protection of their life and property, etc. 26. Bengaluru Urban and others, (2021) 15 SCC 730 and made an observation in paragraph-11 as follows:- Furthermore, the counsels for Appellant have rightly pointed out Rule 21(2)(i) of the Bihar Senior Citizens Rules, 2012 which specifically provides that it is the duty of the District Magistrate to ensure that the life and property of the senior citizens are protected and they are able to live with security and dignity.
